Detect Evil.description: A church inquisitor gains the ability to use detect evil at will as a spell-like ability.

Discern Lies.description: At 9th level, a church inquisitor can use discern lies as a spell-like ability up to three times per day.

Force Shapechange.description: Beginning at 6th level, a church inquisitor can compel a creature to revert to its true form. The inquisitor must succeed on a melee touch attack against the target. On a successful touch, the inquisitor makes a caster level check as though casting dispel magic against the shapechanging effect. The +4 bonus on dispel checks from the Inquisition domain granted power applies to this check. This ability can reverse the effects of alter self, polymorph, shapechange, and alternate form abilities, regardless of whether they are extraordinary, spell-like, or supernatural in nature. Once reverted, the affected creature is unable to change shape again for 1d6 rounds. The church inquisitor may use this ability at will.

Immune to Charms.description: Starting at 2nd level, a church inquisitor becomes completely immune to all enchantment (charm) spells and effects.

Immune to Compulsions.description: At 5th level, a church inquisitor gains complete immunity to all compulsion spells and effects.

Immunity to Possession.description: At 8th level, a church inquisitor becomes immune to magic jar, soul bind, trap the soul, a ghost's malevolence ability, and all other spells or effects that would displace or supplant the character's life force. The character may still willingly travel to other planes through astral projection.

Inquisition Domain.description: When a character enters this prestige class, he gains access to the Inquisition domain. He receives the domain's granted power (a +4 bonus on dispel checks) and may select spells from that domain as his daily domain spell choices.

Learn the Truth.description: At 10th level, a church inquisitor can compel honesty by touching a creature that has lied to him. The target may attempt a Will save (DC 10 + the inquisitor's class level + his Charisma modifier) to resist this mind-affecting compulsion. On a failed save, the creature must speak the truthful version of the lie it told. This ability can be used 3 times per day.

Pierce Disguise.description: The church inquisitor receives a +4 competence bonus on Spot checks made to see through mundane disguises created with the Disguise skill.

Pierce Illusion.description: At 3rd level, the church inquisitor gains a supernatural ability that allows him to see through illusions and magical disguises at will. Whenever the inquisitor observes any illusion or disguise spell, he immediately receives a Will saving throw to penetrate it. He does not need to touch or otherwise interact with the illusion; merely seeing it is sufficient to trigger the save.

Spells per Day/Spells Known.description: The church inquisitor continues to develop divine spellcasting alongside inquisitorial training. Each time the character gains a new level in this prestige class, he receives additional divine spells per day (and spells known, where applicable) as though he had also advanced one level in a divine spellcasting class he belonged to before entering this prestige class. He does not, however, receive any other class benefits that would normally accompany such a level increase (such as improved undead turning or additional uses of special abilities). Effectively, the character adds his church inquisitor level to his existing divine caster level when calculating spells per day. If the character had multiple divine casting classes prior to becoming a church inquisitor, he must select which class benefits from the advancement at each new level.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This prestige class does not grant any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.

classFeatures.description: A church inquisitor continues advancing in divine spellcasting ability as well as learning the skills of inquisition. Thus, when a new church inquisitor level is gained, the character gains new divine spells per day (and spells known, if applicable) as if he had also gained a level in whatever divine spellcasting class he belonged to before he added the prestige class. He does not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained (improved chance of controlling or rebuking undead, more frequent remove disease, and so on). This means that he adds the level of church inquisitor to the level of another divine spellcasting class the character has, then determines spells per day accordingly. If a character had more than one divine spellcasting class before he became a church inquisitor, the player must decide which class to assign each level of church inquisitor for the purpose of determining divine spells per day and spells known.
